name: libaribcaption
why: Decodes ARIB Japanese broadcast captions from transport streams, a real door into obscure broadcast standards.

brief.what_it_is: libaribcaption is a portable C++17 library, with a C API, that decodes and renders ARIB STD-B24 captions, the closed-caption system used in Japanese ISDB TV broadcasting. It is meant to be embedded in video players. The README does not name its input format explicitly. It points to a sample with ffmpeg, which suggests caption data is taken from a demuxed broadcast stream. Output is rendered caption graphics, and the README says the goal is to match or beat how a television displays these captions. It supports Japanese (ARIB JIS), Latin (ABNT NBR 15606-1) and Philippine UTF-8 caption variants.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says ARIB captions are still poorly supported by general video players even though ISDB broadcasting has run for about 20 years. The library aims to let those players render ARIB captions with the same effect as a TV, or better.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not describe the internal pipeline in detail. It says the library provides a decoder and a renderer, with pluggable text backends: DirectWrite on Windows, CoreText on macOS and iOS, and FreeType or Fontconfig elsewhere. It also includes built-in font fallback, support for ARIB gaiji (additional symbols) and DRCS characters, and a built-in table that maps known DRCS characters to alternative Unicode. Graphics rendering is SSE2-optimised on x86/x64.

commands_seen.context: Enter the cloned source directory before building.
Configure a Release build from inside build/.
Compile the library using 8 parallel jobs.
Install the built library system-wide; the README marks this step as optional.
Configure a build that produces a shared library instead of the default static one. The README also lists -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS:BOOL=ON as an alternative.
Windows XP configuration from the README. Note that the first option is written as -A rather than -D in the source, so it may be a typo. Copied verbatim as published.
Link a C program against the static library through pkg-config. The README also shows a version without --static for the shared library.

brief.install_notes: Requires CMake 3.28 or newer and a C++17 compiler. The default build is static. Options include ARIBCC_BUILD_TESTS, ARIBCC_NO_RENDERER (decoder only), ARIBCC_USE_FREETYPE, ARIBCC_USE_EMBEDDED_FREETYPE (fetches and builds a static FreeType automatically, for environments like Android NDK or Windows), and ARIBCC_USE_FONTCONFIG. On Windows and macOS the library needs no third-party dependencies by default. On Linux it needs libfreetype and libfontconfig. Consumers can use find_package(aribcaption), add_subdirectory(), or pkg-config. The README also recommends installing one of several Japanese fonts for good results: Windows TV MaruGothic, Hiragino Maru Gothic ProN on macOS, Rounded M+ 1m for ARIB, or 和田研中丸ゴシック2004ARIB.
brief.standout: It is one of the few portable, MIT-licensed ARIB decoders with a renderer, and it can run with no third-party dependencies on Windows and macOS. It also handles gaiji and DRCS glyphs and maps known DRCS characters to Unicode with a built-in table. Its README says it was heavily inspired by aribb24, aribb24.js and TVCaptionMod2.
brief.status: unknown. The README has no release dates, version numbers, changelog or commit information, and the fetch returned only the README. It is a reasonably complete project page, but I could not confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: Requires CMake 3.28+ and C++17. The README says Windows XP support needs DirectWrite turned off, 'which will result in a crash', and this path also needs GDI and FreeType. Android 2.x support requires FreeType. The recommended Japanese fonts are third-party downloads and not bundled, and some are community projects. The README is written in English with a Japanese translation, and I did not fetch the Japanese version. The input container format is not stated in the README.
quotes: A portable caption decoder / renderer for handling ARIB STD-B24 based TV broadcast captions.
making it possible for general players to render ARIB captions with the same effect (or even better) as Television.
Though ISDB-based TV broadcasting has been operating for about 20 years, ARIB based caption is still lacking support in general players.

judge.reason: A portable decoder for Japan’s broadcast-caption standard opens a genuinely unusual rabbit hole into broadcast text, gaiji, and custom glyphs.

entry.title: libaribcaption
entry.tldr: A C++ library that decodes and renders ARIB STD-B24, the closed-caption system of Japanese digital TV, so video players can display captions as a television does.
entry.deeper_look:
libaribcaption is a portable C++17 library with a C API. It decodes ARIB STD-B24 captions, the caption format used in Japanese ISDB broadcasting, and renders them as graphics. It is meant to be embedded in video players rather than run on its own. The README points to an ffmpeg-based sample, which suggests the caption data comes from a demuxed broadcast stream, but it does not name the input format.

The README says why it exists: "Though ISDB-based TV broadcasting has been operating for about 20 years, ARIB based caption is still lacking support in general players." The aim is to render ARIB captions "with the same effect (or even better) as Television." Supported variants are Japanese (ARIB JIS), Latin (ABNT NBR 15606-1) and Philippine UTF-8.

The interesting part is how far a broadcast caption system sits from plain subtitles. ARIB captions use additional symbols called gaiji and custom glyphs called DRCS, and the library ships a built-in table that maps known DRCS characters to alternative Unicode. Text drawing is pluggable: DirectWrite on Windows, CoreText on macOS and iOS, FreeType and Fontconfig elsewhere, with font fallback built in. It credits aribb24, aribb24.js and TVCaptionMod2 as inspirations.

This is a library, so there is no command to run. The entry point is building it, reading the headers, and linking a small C program against it. It is a door into a broadcast standard few people outside Japan ever see.
entry.install:
brew install libaribcaption
# Library only, no executables. Building from source needs CMake 3.28+ and a C++17 compiler. On Linux it needs libfreetype and libfontconfig. A Japanese font such as Rounded M+ 1m for ARIB is recommended for good rendering.

try_this.what_happens: Configures a Release build from inside a build/ directory in the cloned source.
Compiles the library with 8 parallel jobs, producing a static library by default.
Links your own C program against the static library through pkg-config.

entry.whats_unique: It is one of the few portable, MIT-licensed ARIB decoders that also includes a renderer, and on Windows and macOS it needs no third-party dependencies by default.
entry.caveats: It is a library with no executables, the README gives no release dates so recent activity is unconfirmed, and the input container format is not stated.
